6	import Mathlib

8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSheaf
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivFunctorDef
10	
11	/-!
12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field — it is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302), and a
44	representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology. So an
45	unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a **false** statement, not
46	merely an unproved one. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
47	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
48	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
49	
50	```
51	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
52	```
53	
54	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
55	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
56	both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
57	the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
58	of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
59	declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
60	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
61	`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)
62	
63	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
64	
65	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
66	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
67	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
68	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
69	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
70	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
71	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
72	
73	## Main results
74	
75	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
76	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
77	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
78	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
79	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,

860	It follows from `HasPicScheme` — the representing witness is
861	`Classical.choose`-extracted, so its `choose_spec` is exactly this statement.
862	The class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer signature of
863	`representable`. -/
864	class PicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
865	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
866	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
867	  has_representable : Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C))
868	
869	/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
870	`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
871	of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
872	`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
873	separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `fgaPicardRepresentability`. -/
874	instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
875	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
876	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
877	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
878	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩
879	
880	/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**
881	
882	Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
883	`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
884	point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
885	the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection
886	
887	```
888	(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
889	```
890	
891	for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
892	against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
893	(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
894	with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/
895	noncomputable def representable {k : Type u} [Field k]
896	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
897	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
898	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] [PicSharpRepresentable C] :
899	    (picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C) :=

899	    (picSharp C).RepresentableBy (PicScheme C) :=
900	  Classical.choice (PicSharpRepresentable.has_representable (C := C))
901	
902	/-! ## §5. The abelian group-scheme structure
903	
904	The Picard scheme `Pic_{C/k}` inherits an abelian group-scheme structure from
905	the tensor product of invertible sheaves on `C ×_k T`: the relative Picard
906	presheaf is group-valued (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), and a representing object
907	of (the set-valued shadow of) a group-valued presheaf is canonically a group
908	object, by Yoneda transport (`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`).
909	
910	Since `picSharp` is by definition `relPresheaf ⋙ forget`, the transport
911	applies directly.
912	
913	Blueprint reference: `thm:pic_is_group_scheme` (Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs` +
914	§4 Def. `df:Psch`). -/
915	
916	/-- The multiplicative (`CommGrpCat`-valued) avatar of the relative Picard
917	presheaf, used to feed `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (whose API is
918	multiplicative). Carrier-level it is the same functor: `Multiplicative` is a
919	type synonym. -/
920	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrp {k : Type u} [Field k]
921	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
922	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
923	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
924	  PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.toCommGrp
925	
926	/-- The set-valued shadows of `picSharpCommGrp` and `picSharp` agree up to
927	the canonical `Multiplicative.ofAdd` bijection (a natural isomorphism, since
928	`Multiplicative` is carrier-preserving). -/
929	noncomputable def picSharpCommGrpForgetIso {k : Type u} [Field k]
930	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
931	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
932	    picSharp C ≅ picSharpCommGrp C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget CommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
933	  NatIso.ofComponents
934	    (fun T => Equiv.toIso (Multiplicative.ofAdd
935	      (α := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type (u+1)))))
936	    (fun _ => rfl)
937	
938	/-- **The Picard scheme is a commutative `k`-group scheme** — a canonical
939	`CommGrpObj` structure (i.e. `GrpObj` + `IsCommMonObj`) on `PicScheme C`,
940	obtained by Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the
941	abelian-group structure of the relative Picard presheaf
942	`PicSharp.relPresheaf` along the representability witness `representable C`.
943	Concretely: `[L] + [M] = [L ⊗ M]`, `-[L] = [L⁻¹]`, unit `[O_{C ×_k T}]`,
944	transported through `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`.
945	
946	Commutativity comes for free from the transport, so this is the full
947	abelian-group-scheme statement of the blueprint
948	(`thm:pic_is_group_scheme`). -/
949	noncomputable instance groupSchemeStructure {k : Type u} [Field k]
950	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
951	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
952	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
953	    CommGrpObj (PicScheme C) :=
954	  CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (PicScheme C) (picSharpCommGrp C)
955	    ((representable C).ofIso (picSharpCommGrpForgetIso C))
956	
957	/-! ## §6. Local finiteness of the Picard scheme
958	
959	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): the Picard scheme is separated and locally of
960	finite type over the base. `HasPicScheme` packages local finiteness together
961	with the representability existential (one existence package, as in Kleiman's
962	theorem), so the carrier below is obtained by extraction. It is what the
963	identity-component substrate (`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean`,
964	`GroupScheme.IdentityComponent`) consumes to specialise to
965	`G = PicScheme C`. -/
966	
967	/-- Typeclass asserting that the structural morphism of the Picard scheme is
968	locally of finite type (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): `Pic_{C/k}` is a
969	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes, hence locally of
970	finite type). The `HasPicScheme` existential carries local finiteness, so the
971	property of the `Classical.choose` witness is its second `choose_spec`
972	component; the class survives to preserve the blueprint-pinned consumer
973	signature. -/
974	class PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
975	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
976	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
977	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : Prop where
978	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom
979	
980	/-- Existence instance for `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`: Kleiman §4 Thm
981	`th:main`(1) makes local finiteness part of the same existence package as
982	representability, so the `HasPicScheme` existential carries it and the
983	property of the chosen witness is the second component of its `choose_spec`.
984	The instance hypothesis is `[HasPicScheme C]` rather than
985	`[HasRationalPoint C]`: the rational-point conditionality lives entirely in
986	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (the sole producer of `HasPicScheme C`), and any consumer able
987	to name `PicScheme C` already quantifies over `[HasPicScheme C]`. -/
988	instance instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType {k : Type u} [Field k]
989	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
990	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
991	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
992	    PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C :=
993	  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.1⟩
994	
995	/-- Projection of `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` to the Mathlib morphism
996	property, so that instance search finds `LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme
997	C).hom` whenever the carrier class is in scope (as the identity-component
998	substrate requires). -/
999	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1000	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1001	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
1002	    [PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C] :
1003	    LocallyOfFiniteType (PicScheme C).hom :=
1004	  PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType.locallyOfFiniteType
1005	
1006	/-- **`Pic_{C/k}` is separated over `k`.**
1007	
1008	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main` packages separatedness together with representability
1009	and local finite type for `Pic_{C/k}` ("Then `Pic_{X/k}` is separated, ..."):
1010	one existence package, as in the theorem. As with
1011	`instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, we extract this property from the
1012	strengthened `HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme` existential — its third
1013	component — so downstream files (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) can consume
1014	`IsSeparated (PicScheme C).hom` as a normal instance without opening the axiom
1015	layer. The conditionality on `[HasRationalPoint C]` lives entirely upstream in
1016	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` (the sole producer of `HasPicScheme C`); this extraction only
1017	names `[HasPicScheme C]`, as every consumer able to name `PicScheme C`
1018	already does. -/
1019	instance isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k]
1020	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
1021	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
1022	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] :
1023	    IsSeparated (PicScheme C).hom :=
1024	  (HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.2.2
1025	
1026	end PicScheme

6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicFunctor
8	
9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71	
72	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
74	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
75	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
76	-/
77	
78	set_option autoImplicit false
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory
83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
85	
86	namespace Scheme
87	
88	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
89	
90	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
91	
92	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
93	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
94	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
95	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
96	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
97	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
98	
99	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
100	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
101	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
102	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
103	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
104	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
105	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
106	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
107	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
108	
109	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
110	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
111	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
112	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
113	sieve on the underlying scheme.
114	
115	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
116	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
117	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
118	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
119	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
120	  intro T S hS
121	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
122	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
123	
124	namespace PicSharp
125	
126	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
127	
128	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
129	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
130	
131	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
132	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
133	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
134	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
135	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
136	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
137	
138	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
139	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
140	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
141	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
142	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
143	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
144	
145	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
146	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
147	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
148	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
149	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
150	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
151	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
152	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
153	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
154	
155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property
170	
171	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
178	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
189	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
190	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
194	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
195	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
196	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
197	
198	end PicSharp
199	
200	namespace PicScheme
201	
202	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
203	
204	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
205	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
206	forgotten,
207	
208	```
209	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
210	```
211	
212	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
213	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
214	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
215	`picSharp`.
216	
217	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
218	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
219	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
220	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
221	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
222	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
223	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
224	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
225	
226	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
227	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
228	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.
229	
230	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as
231	`picSharp C`, which is the *same functor by definition* but is declared in the
232	downstream `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (that file imports this one, so
233	the name is not available here). -/
234	noncomputable def picEtComparison {k : Type u} [Field k]
235	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
236	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
237	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} ⟶ picEt C :=
238	  CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskerRight (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C)
239	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1})
240	
241	/-- **`picEt` is an étale sheaf of sets.**
242	
243	The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` survives forgetting the group structure,
244	because the forgetful functor `AddCommGrpCat ⥤ Type` preserves the limits the
245	sheaf condition is stated by. Together with the fact that a representable
246	functor is a sheaf for a subcanonical topology, this is the structural reason
247	the representability obligation is *consistent* as stated — which the
248	unsheafified `picSharp` version was not, absent a rational point. -/
249	theorem picEt_isSheaf_forget {k : Type u} [Field k]
